name: human-sounds
description: Classifies a short audio clip into 10 human non-speech sound classes. YAMNet produces a 1024-value embedding per 0.48 s frame; the frames are averaged and a small dense network trained by the team predicts the class.
architecture: Input(1024) > Dense(512, relu) > Dropout(0.3) > Dense(256, relu) > Dropout(0.3) > Dense(10, softmax)

backbone.name: YAMNet
backbone.use: Frame embeddings averaged over the clip; YAMNet itself is not retrained.

input.normalisation: 16-bit samples divided by 32767, as in the training notebook
input.resampling: scipy.signal.resample (FFT), as in the training notebook

training.data: cleaned_file2.xlsx: 688 labelled rows of ESC-50-style 5-second clips, 385 unique recordings (303 rows are exact duplicates)
training.classOrder: sklearn LabelEncoder (alphabetical), matching the classes list above

reportedMetrics.caveat: The split was made over spreadsheet rows, and 303 of 688 rows are exact duplicates, so test rows can have identical copies in training. Treat these numbers as an upper bound. Run ml/evaluate.py on recordings outside the training list for an honest estimate.
